label: Family holiday gathering

what_happens.title: What happens at the family holiday
goals: A holiday gathering brings family together
There is food, traditions and lots of people
The routine is different for a day or two
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the holiday and tell your child one tradition your family does.

who_is_there.title: Who will be there
goals: Relatives, some well known, some not
Cousins and other kids can be play partners
who_is_there.parentSkill: Look at photos of the relatives together and practise names; agree that a wave or a high five is fine instead of a hug.

what_i_do.title: What I do at the gathering
goals: Take a quiet break when needed
what_i_do.parentSkill: Give your child a small job, like handing out napkins, and agree a quiet spot for breaks.

if_scared.title: If it feels like too much
goals: Holidays can feel loud and busy
Feeling shy or overwhelmed is okay
Calm tools: quiet break, signal, slow breaths
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the overwhelm: 'It's a lot of people. Let's take a break together.'

rehearsal.title: Let's get ready for the holiday
goals: Look at photos and practise names
Practise greetings and the break signal
Choose a job and a comfort item
rehearsal.parentSkill: Play a pretend arrival: toys are relatives, your child chooses a greeting for each.

steps: Get ready with special clothes or decorations
Travel to the family home or welcome guests
Say hello to relatives, maybe with hugs
Help with a small job, like setting the table
Share a big meal and family traditions
Play, open gifts or sing, if the family does that
Say goodbye and go to bed later than usual
sensory: lots of voices talking at once
honestyNotes: Holidays can be loud, long and overwhelming, and a child may not know every relative; never force hugs or kisses and never promise everyone will get along. Routines change and bedtimes are late. Use the family's own holiday name and traditions; keep it inclusive of any faith or culture.

questionButtons.text: Do I have to hug everyone?
fallbackAnswer: No. You can choose a hug, a high five or a wave.
[[GROWNUP]] will help if someone forgets to ask.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you which relatives are coming.
We can look at photos and practise names.

questionButtons.text: What if it is too loud?
fallbackAnswer: Gatherings can be loud. You can take a quiet break with [[GROWNUP]].
We can agree a special signal.

questionButtons.text: What if I don't like the food?
fallbackAnswer: You can try a little, or say no thank you.
There will be something you like.
Yes, [[GROWNUP]] will be there the whole time.
You can always find [[GROWNUP]] if you need help.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you the plan, maybe after the meal or after games.
Bedtime may be late, and that is okay for a special day.
It depends on our family's traditions.
The best part is being together.
[[GROWNUP]] can tell you the story of our holiday.
Every family has its own traditions.

questionButtons.text: What if my cousins don't play with me?
fallbackAnswer: You can ask, can I play too?
Or you can help a grown-up or play with [[GROWNUP]].
[[GROWNUP]] can tell you about anyone who can't come this year.
It is okay to miss them, and we can remember them together.

questionButtons.text: Why do I have to wear special clothes?
fallbackAnswer: Special clothes are a way of making the day feel special.
If they feel itchy, tell [[GROWNUP]], and we can find a comfy layer.

techniques.label: Choosing a greeting
techniques.how: Let your child choose a hug, a high five or a wave.

techniques.label: Photo names
techniques.how: Look at photos of relatives and practise names.

techniques.label: A special signal
techniques.how: Agree a signal for a quiet break.

techniques.label: A quiet spot
techniques.how: Find a quiet room or corner for breaks.

techniques.label: A small job
techniques.how: Give your child a job like napkins or greeting at the door.

techniques.label: A comfy layer
techniques.how: Wear something soft under special clothes.

techniques.label: One small bite
techniques.how: Try a tiny bite of a new dish, no pressure.

techniques.label: A comfort toy
techniques.how: Bring a toy or a book for the slow parts.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Hello my way: hug, high five or wave
Quiet break when I need it

pain: If your clothes hurt or itch, tell me.
If your tummy feels too full, take a break.
body: You can try a little and say no thank you.
Late nights make bodies tired. That is okay.
sensory: It's loud. Let's take a quiet break.
The lights and smells are part of the holiday.
strangers: You can choose how to say hello.
separation: I'm right here the whole time.
Use our signal, and I will come.
unknown: First hello, then dinner, then games.
We will go home after dessert.
safety: You never have to hug if you do not want to.
You can always come to me.
social: Your cousins might like to play.
You can ask, can I play too?
love: I love sharing our traditions with you.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will go to a family holiday gathering.
It is a special day when family comes together.
First [[CHILD]] gets ready, maybe in special clothes.
Then the family travels, or guests arrive at home.
Next everyone says hello, and there may be relatives who visit only sometimes.
Before bed, here is a story about a little mole called Milo.
It was Lantern Night, when all the moles gathered.
First Milo put on his best red scarf.
Then the family walked through the tunnels to Grandma Mole's burrow.
Inside, it was warm and full of voices.
Aunties, uncles and cousins Milo hardly knew were everywhere.
Next they all lit little lanterns together.
After that, there was a long table of root soup and berry cake.
Grandpa told the old story of the first lantern.
It was late when Milo yawned and the family went home.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
After that comes a big meal and family traditions.
There may be games, songs, gifts or prayers, whatever the family does.
Last, it is time to say goodbye, and bedtime is later than usual.
[[CHILD]] can ask [[GROWNUP]], what happens first, and what comes next?

In the story, Milo the mole had a job.
Grandma said, can you put a leaf napkin by every bowl?
Milo walked round the long table, one, two, three, all the way to twenty.
Thank you, Milo, said Grandma.
At dinner, Milo tried a tiny bit of the spicy root soup.
It was too hot, so he had bread and cake instead.
Later the burrow got very loud with singing.
Milo tugged Mama's ear twice, their special signal.
They went to a quiet nook and sat together.
Then Milo was ready to join again.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
Playing with cousins is fun.

There may be many voices, strong smells and bright lights.
Special clothes can feel itchy or tight.
Bedtime is late, and bodies get tired.
Some kids feel shy around relatives.
[[CHILD]] can take slow breaths, smell the flower and blow the candle.
In the story, Milo the mole felt overwhelmed.
Everyone was talking at once, and the lanterns were bright.
His scarf felt itchy, and he was very tired.
Milo's eyes filled with tears.
Mama did not say, it is a happy day, so smile.
Mama said, it is a lot, isn't it, let's have a quiet moment.
They went to a little nook, and Milo took off his scarf.
He smelled a flower slowly, and blew a candle.
Mama hummed a soft song.
After a while, Milo felt calmer.
Worried and brave can happen at the same time.
Sometimes grown-ups disagree or get loud.
It is okay to need a break.
Big feelings can happen on special days.

Holidays mark something important to a family, a season, a story, a faith or a memory.
Traditions are passed down, and each family adds its own twist.
Gatherings can be long, so planning breaks matters.
Relatives often want to hear what kids have been up to.
[[CHILD]] can ask an older relative how the holiday was when they were young.
Big families can have complicated feelings between grown-ups, and that is not a kid's job to fix.
Asking a relative a question about themselves is an easy conversation starter.
Older cousins can be great company and helpers.
Body autonomy means everyone chooses how they say hello, kids included.
[[CHILD]] can prepare one thing to share, like a drawing or a story from school.
Helping with jobs is a good way to feel useful when you don't know everyone.
Trying new dishes politely, even a small bite, is a way of respecting the cook.
Breaks are normal; even grown-ups step outside for air.
Thanking the hosts at the end means a lot to them.
[[CHILD]] can be the family photographer for the day.
Special days come with high expectations, which can make normal feelings seem worse.
Sensory overload from noise and crowds is real and affects grown-ups too.
Missing someone who is not there, or who has died, can feel strong on holidays.
Family tension between adults is never a child's fault.
[[CHILD]] can plan a short walk outside with [[GROWNUP]] during the day.
Knowing who will be there and what will happen makes a long day easier.
Preparing a couple of answers to common questions, like how is school, helps with small talk.
Bringing something to do, like a book or a card game, fills the slow parts.
Agreeing on a leave time sets expectations.
[[CHILD]] can make a card or a small gift for the host.
